beats.text: There's a factory in Japan where robots build other robots, in the dark.
beats.dir: mysterious hook; single read, no repetition

beats.text: FANUC has run lights-out production there since 2001. Its robots can work unsupervised for up to thirty days.
beats.dir: factual, impressed; single read, no repetition

beats.text: No lights. No breaks. No shift changes.
beats.dir: punchy, rhythmic; single read, no repetition

beats.text: In China, Xiaomi opened a dark factory in 2024 built to make about ten million phones a year.
beats.dir: factual, scale; single read, no repetition

beats.text: That sounds like the end of factory jobs. But look closer.
beats.dir: lean in; single read, no repetition

beats.text: People still design the products, program the robots, and fix them when they break.
beats.dir: reassuring, clear; single read, no repetition

beats.text: Robots that run 24/7 are like cruise control: the car keeps going, but someone still has to steer.
beats.dir: vivid comparison; single read, no repetition

beats.text: So the real question isn't robots versus humans. It's which jobs grow around them, and that's our next full video.
beats.dir: teasing payoff; single read, no repetition
